environment.description: Same ASP.NET Core 7.0 application deployed in an Azure App Service (Linux) container with the following layered configuration: (1) The container filesystem uses a read-only root filesystem with an OverlayFS upper layer mounted at /var/app/uploads/extracted with a bind-propagation setting of 'rprivate' and a mount namespace that prevents path traversal beyond the mount point boundary — specifically, the Azure App Service sandbox applies seccomp-bpf profile 'appservice-restricted-v2' which intercepts openat() syscalls and rejects any path resolution containing '..' components that would resolve outside the designated writable mount points; (2) The Content-Security-Policy response header is set via an Azure Front Door Rules Engine rule that appends 'script-src' directives with 'strict-dynamic' and requires all script elements to carry valid SRI hashes matching a pinned allowlist stored in Azure Key Vault, referenced at deploy time — however this CSP is applied as 'Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only' in the current configuration revision (rev-3a); (3) The Azure App Service has a custom startup script that applies an immutable attribute (chattr +i) to all files in /var/app/wwwroot/js/ after deployment, preventing overwrite even by the application user.

config.runtime: dotnet 7.0 on Azure App Service Linux
config.container_sandbox: appservice-restricted-v2 seccomp-bpf profile with openat() path validation
config.filesystem: read-only rootfs, OverlayFS upper at /var/app/uploads/extracted with rprivate propagation
config.mount_namespace: isolated, prevents traversal beyond mount boundaries
config.csp_header: Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only via Azure Front Door Rules Engine (rev-3a)
config.key_vault_sri_pins: SHA-384 hashes pinned in Azure Key Vault secret 'sri-plugin-hashes-v2'
